pamphlet_excerpts: Discuss Forms Humankind Means: Your counselor: The question of what "art" is has occupied the minds ofphilosophers and critics ever since humankind began to think and argue (p. 8).

Discuss Forms Humankind Means Principle 2: Your counselor Principle 2: The term has been applied to many forms of visualmedia, especially to the fine arts, drawing, painting, sculpture, and printmaking (p. 8).
Discuss Forms Humankind Means Principle 3: Your counselor Principle 3: But it also includes architecture, industrialdesign, fashion design, pottery, and weaving (p. 8).

Discuss Forms Humankind Means Principle 4: Your counselor Principle 4: The differenceis that fine arts are concerned only with beauty and expression and the others, though the art may be beautiful, focus firston function (p. 8).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Discuss Forms Humankind Means): Step 1 (Your counselor): This merit badge pamphlet concentrates on two-dimensional art, specifically drawing and painting in various media (p. 8).
Step 2 (Discuss Forms Humankind Means): Step 2 (Your counselor): One requirement introduces you to design applications in thefields of graphic arts and industrial design (p. 8).
Step 3 (Discuss Forms Humankind Means): Step 3 (Your counselor): After you learnabout art history and design principles, you will understandhow these fields relate to fine art (p. 8).
Step 4 (Discuss Forms Humankind Means): Step 4 (Your counselor): Since prehistoric people first madecave paintings, artists have tried to portrayreality (p. 8).

pamphlet_excerpts: Elements of Art and Design Balance Balance is the visual stability of the composition (p. 16).
Elements of Art and Design Principle 2: If a work of art has visual balance, then the viewer feels that the elements have been arranged just right (p. 16).
Elements of Art and Design Principle 3: If there is an imbalance, then the viewer feels something's wrong, that the elementsneed to be rearranged (p. 16).
Elements of Art and Design Principle 4: A formal balance occurs whensimilar elements are placed on eachside of the central axis (a drawn orimaginary line through the center of the work) (p. 16).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Elements of Art and Design): The differentelements of art, line, value, shape, space, color, and texture, all influence the visual weight of a composition (p. 16).
Step 2 (Elements of Art and Design): Forexample, a small area of bright color can balance a larger area of dull color (p. 16).
Step 3 (Elements of Art and Design): Elements of Art and Design Elements of Artand Design When you create art, you are expressing your ideas, your feelings, or your beliefs (p. 16).
Step 4 (Elements of Art and Design): If you intend to share your art with otherpeople, you need to know how to organize your design so thatthey will understand what your art is telling (p. 16).

pamphlet_excerpts: Principles of Design: Six Principles of Design: These principles are guidelines, notrules, to help you express yourself artistically (p. 23).

Principles of Design Principle 4: Six Principles of Design Principle 4: Rhythm indicates movement by the repetition of a certain artelement or combination of elements (p. 23).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Principles of Design): Step 1 (Six Principles of Design): The repeated element, a shape or line, for example, is called a motif (p. 23).
Step 2 (Principles of Design): Step 2 (Six Principles of Design): The artistuses the repetition of a motif to lead the viewer's eye around the work of art (p. 23).
Step 3 (Principles of Design): Step 3 (Six Principles of Design): Random rhythm happenswhen a motif is repeated in noapparent order, with irregularspacing between one motif and the next (p. 23).
Step 4 (Principles of Design): Step 4 (Six Principles of Design): Regular rhythm occurs whenidentical motifs with identicalspacing between them arerepeated (p. 23).
